findings: learner.overview.text: Replace “it may directly represent four” with a clear distinction between early numeral forms written 亖, which are described as directly representing four and as coexisting with forms written 四, and the separate interpretation of some 四 forms as counting rods. Then distinguish both from the competing borrowing proposals: one treats 四 as a breath-related graph associated with 呬, later borrowed for “four,” without establishing the referent’s ancient name; the other proposes 四 was the original graph for 泗 (“nasal discharge”), later borrowed for “four,” and is explicitly said to lack textual attestation. Keep the 囗 enclosure and inner 儿-form strokes explicitly as the present visible structure, not an account of ancient roles. Cite X-e6d62080b1a5fc5178a4, X-7b17032f87fb77433387, X-2723cf5f9190c41c2cfe, X-4b62255296f832195814, and X-741838c69c6335267eb0.

Revise `learner.overview` to distinguish the early numeral graph 亖 from 四: the evidence describes 亖 as directly representing four and says it coexisted with forms written 四. Keep the counting-rod interpretation identified as a proposal about some 四 forms. Then distinguish the separate proposals: 四 as a breath-related graph associated with 呬, later borrowed for “four,” and 四 as the proposed original graph of 泗 (“nasal discharge”), later borrowed for “four,” a proposal lacking textual attestation. Keep the current 囗-enclosing-儿-form description limited to visible structure. Cite these claims with X-e6d62080b1a5fc5178a4, X-7b17032f87fb77433387, X-2723cf5f9190c41c2cfe, and X-4b62255296f832195814.
